headline: High-risk shared-workspace and tool-use pair: Windsurf can write/execute while Plano has broad egress, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files, uses MCP, clipboard, and can auto-execute commands; Plano can emit OpenAI-compatible outputs and broad network egress. A shared file or MCP bridge lets attacker-controlled content from one side influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented beyond workspace-style interaction, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Windsurf ingests Plano-generated text from a shared workspace or MCP channel as instructions, injection is possible.
IF auto-execute is enabled in Windsurf, malicious content from Plano outputs can be operationalized faster.
mitigations: Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Keep Plano and Windsurf on separate workspaces.
Route Plano output through a human review step before any file or MCP ingestion.
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, provenance-tagged sources.
Use read-only exports instead of shared editable files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and have broad network egress; Windsurf also handles workspace files and model-provider keys, while Plano touches logs/metrics/traces and calls an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Shared workspace data can therefore flow into outbound model traffic, creating a realistic leakage path in default use.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains secrets, logs, or source code, Windsurf may read them and send them onward via model proxy or MCP.
IF Plano is pointed at sensitive traces or logs, its outbound API calls can transmit those contents off-host.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
Remove secrets from shared folders before opening them in Windsurf.
Disable or narrow MCP access to approved servers only.
Use redacted logs/traces for Plano inputs.
Rotate any exposed model-provider keys immediately if they were stored in workspace files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Plano has no write or concurrency controls but can still be affected by shared files if both operate on the same repo or workspace. The pair therefore has overlapping mutable-state access with no locking mechanism shown, which matches the high-risk shared-write pattern.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace, concurrent edits can clobber each other.
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while Plano is reading or routing files, state drift can occur without coordination.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the same repo.
Use git branches and frequent commits.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Add a manual lock file or ticketing step before edits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf is an action-taking coding agent with command execution and MCP access; Plano can generate routed outputs over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If Windsurf treats Plano output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes, shell commands, or git commits, making the blast radius high.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes Plano output without verification, incorrect facts can become code or command actions.
IF Plano is used to summarize or route instructions that Windsurf then executes, a single upstream error can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Require human review of Plano outputs before Windsurf acts.
Add schema validation for any Plano-to-Windsurf handoff.
Limit Windsurf to dry-run mode for high-impact commands.
Log and diff all generated edits before commit.
Use explicit provenance labels on Plano outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Windsurf is closed-source and handles model-provider keys plus workspace files; Plano is open-source and documented as an AI gateway with broad egress. The pair can move sensitive code, logs, or traces into a closed-source editor and onward to external model services, but no specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated data such as source code, logs, or traces is opened in Windsurf, it may be processed by a closed-source product and external model services.
IF organizational policy requires open-source-only handling for those data classes, the pair violates that policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf workspaces.
Use a DPA-reviewed environment for any sensitive files.
Store model keys outside the editor workspace.
Document data-class handling rules for both tools.
Prefer redacted or synthetic inputs for Plano.
